item.title: Malaysia Launches Probe Into Srinivasan’s Johor Startup School
item.description: Malaysian authorities have launched an immigration probe into a school for technology startups, just months after investor Balaji Srinivasan pitched the educational facility to officials and called for policies to support the project.

item.title: Philippine Outsourcing Group Cuts Revenue and Jobs Forecasts on AI
item.description: The Philippines’ main business-process outsourcing group cut its industry revenue and job forecasts — and even warned of possible shrinking future business — with the emergence of artificial intelligence, shifting geopolitical conditions and increased competition.

item.title: Traders Boost BOE and ECB Rate-Hike Bets After Oil Price Surge
item.description: Traders boosted wagers on faster Bank of England and European Central Bank interest-rate hikes after surging oil prices reignited inflation fears.

item.title: China Widens Australian Canola Trade to Include Private Crushers
item.description: China will allow its private oilseed crushers to buy Australian canola, as the two countries move to normalize a trade that’s largely been halted since the start of the decade.

item.title: Rathbones Cut Gilt Exposure in Case Burnham ‘Does a Truss’
item.description: Rathbones Asset Management has reduced its holdings of UK government bonds to avoid a potential selloff if Andy Burnham boosts spending and raises borrowing.

item.title: Byju’s Founder Loses Bid to Overturn Singapore Jail Sentence
item.description: The High Court of Singapore rejected a bid by the founder of failed education startup Byju’s to overturn a six-month jail sentence, effectively barring him from returning to the city-state unless he’s prepared to serve the term.

item.title: China’s Trade Surplus With EU Hits Record as Tensions Intensify
item.description: China’s trade surplus with the European Union climbed to a fresh high, keeping the issue of growing imbalances high on the agenda as the bloc weighs new measures to shield local industries.

item.title: Klarna Plans New Buy-Now-Pay-Later SRT as It Targets US Growth
item.description: Klarna is seeking to offload credit risk tied to a portfolio of ‘buy now, pay later loans’, in a deal aimed at freeing up capital as it looks to accelerate its international expansion plans.

item.title: Samsung Is Said in Early Discussions on Potential US Share Sale
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. is in the early stages of exploring a potential offering of American depositary receipts, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Trillion Dollar Chip Rout Trains Spotlight on TSMC and ASML Results
item.description: At a time of acute investor unease over a selloff in AI-inflated tech stocks, this week’s results from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and ASML Holding NV carry even greater significance than usual.

item.title: Middle East War Set to Push Back LNG Glut by a Year, BNEF Says
item.description: The liquefied natural gas market will move into oversupply in 2028, a year later than previously forecast, as war in the Middle East and major project delays push back the emergence of a global glut, according to BloombergNEF.

item.title: Deutsche Bank and World Bank Team Up for Trade Finance Platform
item.description: The World Bank and Deutsche Bank AG are starting a €1 billion trade finance platform for frontier and emerging markets.

item.title: Improving Hiring Trends Boost Embattled European Recruiters
item.description: European staffing companies’ better-than-feared numbers and cautiously optimistic outlook are pointing to a stabilizing labor market after years of downturn.

item.title: Indian Insurers Ask for Wider Use of Swaps to Hedge Rate Risks
item.description: Some Indian insurers are asking regulators to allow them to use more interest-rate hedging tools as they prepare to play a larger role in the country’s money markets, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Asian Oil Buyers Look to US Crude as Iran War Intensifies
item.description: The escalation of hostilities between Washington and Tehran and the virtual standstill in observable traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is prompting Asian refiners to look at buying more US oil.

item.title: Ashmore Sees $1.3 Billion of Inflows as Clients Embrace EM Funds
item.description: Ashmore Group Plc reported net inflows for the three months through June as the emerging-markets-focused asset manager’s funds performed well with markets roiled by the uncertainty sparked by the war in Iran.

item.title: BP Flags $1 Billion Writedown From Low Carbon Business
item.description: BP Plc said it expects to write down another $1 billion from energy transition assets in the second quarter, as the British major continues the painstaking work of re-orientating itself toward its core oil and gas business.

item.title: Nvidia Partner GMI Cloud Seeks $635 Million GPU-Backed Bank Loan
item.description: US-based data center operator GMI Cloud is seeking a NT$20.45 billion ($635 million) multi-tranche loan deal supported by customer contracts for graphics processing units, one of the first such financings in Asia that reflects the region’s growing demand for artificial intelligence.

item.title: Europe Is Set for the Strongest Earnings Growth in Three Years
item.description: European companies are set to post their strongest profit growth in three years in the second-quarter reporting season, buoyed by expected blowout results from oil majors, banks and artificial intelligence winners.

item.title: India Inflation Risks Mount on Renewed US-Iran Tensions, El Nino
item.description: India’s stronger-than-expected inflation reading for June has left policymakers facing a more uncertain outlook, with renewed tensions around the Strait of Hormuz threatening to push up oil prices and a developing El Niño raising the risk of higher food costs.

item.title: Finland’s NestAI Builds Sovereign AI Tools for Europe Militaries
item.description: Finnish artificial intelligence lab NestAI Oy is launching an AI engine that the Finnish and Estonian militaries will use to create sovereign models for planning operations and enabling uncrewed autonomous systems.

item.title: Stocks Steady as Oil Extends Gain to $85
India’s Antitrust Body Fines HP $13.3 Million for Cartelizing
item.description: India’s antitrust regulator fined the Indian unit of HP Inc. 1.27 billion rupees ($13.3 million), saying the company colluded with its resellers to rig prices in government procurement tenders.

item.title: Ericsson Sees Higher Quarterly Costs on Network Sales Growth
item.description: Ericsson AB warned that margins for its main networks business will come under pressure this quarter as the Swedish telecommunications maker grapples with higher component costs.

item.title: PE Fund Harith Gets Antitrust Approval to Acquire FlySafair
item.description: South Africa’s antitrust regulator approved private equity firm Harith General Partners’ proposal to acquire budget carrier FlySafair.

item.title: UK’s Miliband Seen as Least Appealing Chancellor: Markets Pulse
item.description: Andy Burnham has yet to announce his choice for UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, but among the presumptive next prime minister’s leading candidates, Energy Secretary Ed Miliband is seen as the least market-friendly choice, according to the latest Bloomberg Markets Live Pulse survey.

item.title: Pure DC Building Finland AI Data Center, Secures Microsoft Deal
item.description: Oaktree Capital Management-backed UK firm Pure Data Centres is building a data center in Finland that clients including Microsoft Corp. are slated to use, part of a broader effort to ramp up the digital infrastructure necessary for Europe to build and run more artificial intelligent systems.

item.title: China’s Green-Tech Exports Surge on Energy Transition Demand
item.description: China’s exports of green-tech products rose by more than a third in the first half of the year, driven by the accelerating global energy transition.

item.title: Indonesia Says S&P Affirmation to Help Stabilize Bond Market
item.description: Indonesia expects S&P Global Ratings’ vote of confidence in its sovereign credit profile to help stabilize the domestic bond market after a selloff in June, according to a top finance ministry official.

item.title: China Expels Former Politburo Member Over Graft and Sex Charges
item.description: China expelled former Politburo member Ma Xingrui from the ruling Communist Party, accusing him of a wide range of offenses including corruption, abuse of power and trading political favors for sex.
